Board src master now lives at Windows scratch `...\scratchpad\board_st7789.c` (pull/edit/push via Windows:9100 http server).
80	- **PHASE 2 (in progress): DVP capture. Big win — NuttX has its own GDMA driver + LCD_CAM, so DON'T port IDF's DMA stack.** Reuse NuttX API (`#include "esp32s3_dma.h"`, clean header no soc/soc.h): `esp32s3_dma_request(ESP32S3_DMA_PERIPH_LCDCAM /*=5*/, tx_prio, rx_prio, burst_en)` -> chan; `esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk(chan,false,ESP32S3_DMA_EXT_MEMBLK_64B)` (PSRAM); `esp32s3_dma_setup(desc,num,buf,len,false/*RX*/,chan)`; `esp32s3_dma_load(desc,chan,false)`; `esp32s3_dma_enable(chan,false)`; `esp32s3_dma_wait_idle(chan,false)`. Desc struct `esp32s3_dmadesc_s{ctrl,pbuf,next}`, max 4095 B/desc. Template = `esp32s3_lcd.c` (flip TX->RX, LCD_*->CAM_*). Pattern: `periph_module_enable(PERIPH_LCD_CAM_MODULE)` OR raw SYSTEM. Pins via `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_in(pin, idx, inv)` (in esp32s3_gpio.h). Cache: after RX DMA, `extern int cache_invalidate_addr(uint32_t addr,uint32_t size);` before reading the PSRAM buffer.
81	- **Phase-2 hardcoded register facts (soc/soc.h off board path, so hardcode):** LCD_CAM base **0x60041000**: CAM_CTRL=+0x4, CAM_CTRL1=+0x8, CAM_RGB_YUV=+0xc, LC_DMA_INT_ENA=+0x64, _ST=+0x6c, _CLR=+0x70. CAM_CTRL fields: STOP_EN b0, VSYNC_FILTER_THRES[3:1], UPDATE_REG b4, BYTE_ORDER b5, BIT_ORDER b6, LINE_INT_EN b7, VS_EOF_EN b8, CLKM_DIV_NUM[16:9], CLK_SEL[30:29](=3 for 160MHz). CAM_CTRL1 fields: REC_DATA_BYTELEN[15:0](=framebytes-1), LINE_INT_NUM[21:16], CLK_INV b22, VSYNC_FILTER_EN b23, 2BYTE_EN b24, DE_INV b25, HSYNC_INV b26, VSYNC_INV b27, VH_DE_MODE_EN b28, START b29, RESET b30, AFIFO_RESET b31. GPIO-matrix INPUT idx: CAM_DATA_IN0=133 (D0..D7 =133..140), CAM_PCLK=149, CAM_H_ENABLE(HREF)=150, CAM_V_SYNC=152. SYSTEM LCD_CAM clk: PERIP_CLK_EN1(0x600C001C) bit8, PERIP_RST_EN1(0x600C0024) bit8. Board DVP pins (velapaw-hardware): VSYNC=17 HREF=18 PCLK=41 D0=45 D1=47 D2=48 D3=46 D4=42 D5=40 D6=39 D7=21 (XCLK=38 already LEDC).
82	- **OV5640 config sequence (port from `sensors/ov5640.c` + `ov5640_settings.h`, all via SCCB 16-bit-reg writes):** (1) `write 0x3008=0x82` sw-reset + 100ms; (2) write the whole `sensor_default_regs[]` array (~180 pairs, handles REG_DLY 0xffff=delay-ms, REGLIST_TAIL 0x0000=end); (3) `set_pll(...)` writes 0x3034=0x1A,0x3035,0x3036,0x3037,0x3108,0x3824,0x460C,0x3103=0x13 — PLL params set PCLK; (4) pixformat RGB565 = `sensor_fmt_rgb565`: **FORMAT_CTRL 0x501F=0x01, FORMAT_CTRL00 0x4300=0x61**; (5) `set_framesize` = windowing writes X_ADDR_ST/END(0x3800..0x3807), **X_OUTPUT_SIZE 0x3808/0x380A = w/h**, X_TOTAL_SIZE(0x380C), X_OFFSET(0x3810), ISP scale bit 0x5001; needs the `resolution[]`+`ratio_table` from ov5640.c for a chosen size (QVGA 320x240). (6) `set_image_options`: **SELFIE MIRROR = write TIMING_TC_REG21 (0x3821) |= 0x06 (hmirror) + reg 0x4514=0xbb** (h-mirror case); vflip = 0x3820|=0x06. In-sensor hmirror is the clean selfie flip (or do it in software `sx=CAM_W-1-...`). Also enable color-bar TEST via 0x503D=0xC0 for a lens-independent capture sanity check.
83	- **PHASE 2 CAPTURE WORKS (2026-07-07) — OV5640 color-bar test pattern captured & VISIBLE ON THE PANEL.** The full custom DVP stack works: LEDC XCLK -> OV5640 SCCB QVGA-RGB565 config -> LCD_CAM camera mode -> NuttX GDMA RX -> PSRAM -> bit-bang blit. Recognizable colors (red/green/white/magenta/blue) = DVP path + RGB565 format fundamentally correct. All code is in the board file `esp32s3_st7789.c` (funcs: `ov5640_wr`, `ov_default_regs[]`, `ov5640_config_qvga`, `cam_pins_init`, `cam_lcdcam_init`, `cam_dma_init`, `cam_capture_once`, `cam_blit`, `cam_capture_test`). **REQUIRED CONFIG: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_DMA=y`** (else `esp32s3_dma_*` undefined at link). Working CAM_CTRL = `(3<<29)|(8<<9)|(4<<1)` (clk_sel=3, clkm_div=8, vsync_filter_thres=4); CAM_CTRL1 = `0xffff | (1<<23)`; NuttX GDMA: `esp32s3_dma_request(ESP32S3_DMA_PERIPH_LCDCAM,0,1,true)` gave chan 0, buf in PSRAM (0x3c0c0040), 38 descs; `cache_invalidate_addr` before reading.
84	- **PHASE 2b DONE — CLEAN full-frame capture (2026-07-07):** vertical color bars, no banding/shear, fill the frame. FIX = **VSYNC-sync + vs_eof**: `cam_wait_vsync()` polls the VSYNC pad level directly (`(rreg(0x6000403C /*GPIO_IN_REG*/) >> 17) & 1`; wait high-pulse then low = frame start), then reset AFIFO + arm the GDMA at that frame start, with **CAM_CTRL vs_eof_en=1** so the DMA runs to the next VSYNC = exactly one aligned frame. (Earlier: no-sync no-vs_eof gave shear/banding = over-capture of >1 frame; vs_eof without sync gave a partial frame.) Capture is now solid.
85	- **COLOR mapping still off** (bars show scrambled colors; white+green right, others swapped). Flipping the blit byte order (p[x]/p[x+1]) did NOT change it → it's a **channel (R/B) or sensor format** thing, NOT blit byte order. Defer to phase 3: fix in the RGB565->RGB888 conversion (extract R/G/B, remap channels) against a REAL scene, or try sensor FORMAT_CTRL00=0x6F vs 0x61 / CAM_CTRL byte_order bit5. Not a blocker. 
86	- **lcdfb OVERWRITES boot-time bit-bang blits:** a blit done in `board_lcd_initialize` gets painted over ~instantly by the `lcdfb`/`/dev/fb0` initial flush of stale PSRAM (the persistent medium-blue = last velapaw LVGL screen). To SEE a boot capture I added a TEMP `up_mdelay(15000)` after `cam_capture_test` in board_lcd_initialize (REMOVE it later). Real visualization = go through `/dev/fb0` / the velapaw preview (phase 3).
87	- **PHASE 3 DONE — LIVE OV5640 CAMERA WORKING IN VELAPAW ON HARDWARE (2026-07-08).** Real recognizable image in the Enroll/Recognize preview, live-updating, enrollment captures real thumbnails. Architecture: board exposes globals `board_ov5640_init(i2c)` (config once at boot, called from board_lcd_initialize after panel_init) + `board_ov5640_capture(uint8_t**buf,int*w,int*h)` (VSYNC-synced grab into g_cambuf). App HAL `hal/camera_ov5640.c` (swapped for camera_mock.c in the velapaw Makefile CSRCS) externs board_ov5640_capture (**FLAT build → app can call board fns directly**), downscales 320x240 RGB565 -> 128x128 RGB888 with selfie mirror (`mx=(w-1)-sx`). **KEY FIX: RGB565 is BIG-ENDIAN in the capture buffer — assemble `px=(p[0]<<8)|p[1]`** (little-endian gave a rainbow scramble). Removed the temp 15s hold + boot blit. **`FRAME_INTERVAL_MS=150`** in ui_lvgl.c for the live preview (was 1000 for the static mock; the event-driven-only preview from the speed pass FROZE the live feed — restored the periodic `if((tab==0||tab==1)&&now-last_frame>...)` grab in the main loop).
88	- **FLASH GOTCHA (cost ~8 failed attempts):** the ESP32-S3 native USB (VID_303A/PID_1001) started giving pyserial **"Write timeout"** on every flash after heavy velapaw/camera use. Cable swap, full power-cycle, `--before usb-reset`, killing stray python, and PnP disable/enable ALL FAILED — **the fix was a DIFFERENT PC USB port** (front-panel/hub port had weak data lines). Flash from a rear/motherboard port.
89	- **CAMERA POLISH DONE (2026-07-08):** (1) **tearing fixed** — `cam_capture_once` now waits for the frame-END VSYNC (`cam_wait_vsync()` after arming the DMA) instead of a fixed `up_mdelay(80)`; a fixed delay races the frame time and gives torn/shifted-band frames when the scene moves. (2) **scroll smoothness** — the blocking per-frame capture made scrolling sluggish; fixed by (a) pausing capture while a finger is down: `ui_touch_active()` in ui_lvgl.c (`lv_indev_get_next`/`lv_indev_get_state`==LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED) gating the preview grab, and (b) disabling scroll momentum/elastic on all 4 tab pages (`lv_obj_clear_flag(tab, LV_OBJ_FLAG_SCROLL_MOMENTUM|LV_OBJ_FLAG_SCROLL_ELASTIC)`) — the post-release glide was many slow bit-bang repaints. Residual scroll heaviness is the bit-bang panel floor (parked SPI2 fix).
90	- **REMAINING:** real recognition needs TFLM INT8 (identity+BCS) on LX7 — see TFLM section below. Optional: verify exact R/B channel order + mirror direction against a real pet; auto-start velapaw on boot. Masters: board `...\scratchpad\board_st7789.c`, HAL `...\scratchpad\camera_ov5640.c`, UI on D:; refs `...\scratchpad\esp32cam\` + `...\scratchpad\nxcam\`.
91	
92	## TFLM (tflite-micro) on esp32s3 — build recipe (2026-07-08)
93	**tflite-micro is a real buildable package** at `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro` (`CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO`). Models present at `apps/examples/velapaw/infer/model/`: **velapaw.tflite = 1.4 MB (a REAL embedding model, NOT the person_detect placeholder — the "placeholder" comment in backend_tflm.cc is STALE)**, bcs.tflite = 612 KB. `generate_cc_arrays.py` (model→C array) is at `.../tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/`.
94	**IT COMPILES for esp32s3** after these fixes (the hard part — done; ~7 issues solved in sequence):
95	1. **defconfig deps:** `CONFIG_SYSTEM_FLATBUFFERS=y CONFIG_MATH_GEMMLOWP=y CONFIG_MATH_KISSFFT=y CONFIG_MATH_RUY=y CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO=y` (TFLITEMICRO depends on all 4).
96	2. **C++ lib:** switch `CONFIG_LIBCXXNONE` → **`CONFIG_LIBCXXTOOLCHAIN=y`** (NONE has no `<new>`/C++ headers).
97	3. **`CONFIG_LIBM=y`** (else NuttX `<math.h>` doesn't declare global math → NuttX's `include/cxx/cmath` shim `using ::round` etc. all fail).
98	4. In `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile` COMMON_FLAGS: add **`-DTF_LITE_USE_GLOBAL_CMATH_FUNCTIONS`** (use `::round`/`::expm1` not `std::`).
99	5. Add **`CXXFLAGS += -fpermissive`** (double→float function-pointer conversions in unused elementwise ops).
100	6. Patch `tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/kernels/internal/{max,min}.h`: `std::fmax/fmin` → `(x>y)?x:y` / `(x<y)?x:y` (not in NuttX std::).
101	7. **KEY:** NuttX `<cmath>` shim has NO float overloads (`std::exp(float)`→double), breaking lambda→`float(*)(float)` conversions (elementwise + softmax LUT). FIX = force-include a **float-overload shim**: create `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/float_shim.h` (`namespace std { inline float exp(float x){return expf(x);} ... sqrt/log/log2/sin/cos/tanh/round/floor/ceil/fabs/pow/fmax/fmin/fmod/expm1 }`) and add `CXXFLAGS += -include $(APPDIR)/mlearning/tflite-micro/float_shim.h`.
102	**TFLITE-MICRO NOW BUILDS + LINKS CLEAN into nuttx.bin (2026-07-08).** The link failures were build-tree inconsistency from the many incremental config changes (corrupt staging/*.a "no more archived files"; then a 131 MB libapps.a with MULTIPLE mismatched LVGL variants lvgl/lvgl_4/lvgl_6 -> undefined lv_image_decoder_*/lv_draw_buf_*). **FIX = clean rebuild** (`cd nuttx && make clean` keeps .config; `rm -rf staging/*.a`; then `./build.sh ...`; recompiles tflite ~15-20 min; re-apply fix_hal for esp-hal). One more shim fix needed: **remove `pow` from float_shim.h** — `std::pow(2,15)` (int literals) is ambiguous between the shim's float pow and global double pow (the other 15 shim overloads are fine). After the clean rebuild + pow removal: BUILD OK. NOTE the binary is unchanged size (680656 B) because nothing references tflite-micro yet -> linker drops it as dead code; it's PROVEN to build but not in the image until velapaw's backend is wired.
103	**VELAPAW TFLM BACKEND WIRED + LINKED WITH THE REAL 1.4MB MODEL (2026-07-08): nuttx.bin = 2.18 MB** (up from 680 KB → model + tflite code now in the image). Steps that worked: (1) generate model C-array: `python3 <tflm>/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/generate_cc_arrays.py velapaw/infer/gen/velapaw_model_data.cc velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite` (+ .h) — array name derives from OUTPUT name → `g_velapaw_model_data` (matches backend). (2) backend_tflm.cc: arena `static uint8_t g_arena[768K]` → `uint8_t *g_arena=nullptr` + `kmm_memalign(16,kArenaSize)` in tflm_init (`#include <nuttx/kmalloc.h>`) — PSRAM, too big for internal .bss. (3) velapaw Makefile TFLM block (ifeq CONFIG_VELAPAW_INFER_TFLM): `CXXEXT:=.cc`, `CXXSRCS += infer/backend_tflm.cc infer/gen/velapaw_model_data.cc`, `CSRCS += assets/velapaw_assets.c` (ui_lvgl.c #includes velapaw_assets.h under TFLM), include paths for velapaw root + gen + assets + tflite-micro + gemmlowp/kissfft/ruy on **BOTH CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS** (app-root `-I.../examples/velapaw` on CXXFLAGS was the missed one → "infer/infer.h not found"), and `-DTFLITE_EMULATE_FLOAT -DTF_LITE_DISABLE_X86_NEON -DTF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS -DTF_LITE_USE_GLOBAL_CMATH_FUNCTIONS`. (4) defconfig: `CONFIG_VELAPAW_INFER_TFLM=y`, `CONFIG_VELAPAW_INFER_TFLM_ARENA_SIZE=786432`, and **`CONFIG_TLS_NELEM=8`** (was 0 → libsupc++ eh_globals undefined `pthread_key_create/getspecific/setspecific/key_delete`). BCS left OFF (VELAPAW_HAVE_BCS undefined) for this first pass.
104	**FLASHED (2.18MB) + BOOTS OK, but velapaw HANGS in tflm_init at model access (2026-07-08).** Diagnosed with printf traces in backend_tflm.cc (printf works; MicroPrintf is stripped by -DTF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS so tflm's own logs are invisible). Sequence seen: `arena alloc 786432 B` OK → `arena=0x3c2a0850` (768KB PSRAM alloc fine) → `GetModel...` → **HANG** (never reaches `model version=`). So it faults/hangs on first access to the 1.4MB model flatbuffer (`tflite::GetModel()` / `g_model->version()`). NOT stack (bumped to 131072, no help), NOT arena. **REFINED DIAGNOSIS (raw-read trace): model IS reachable + aligned — NOT an alignment fault.** Trace prints `GetModel... data@0x3c045e90 [0..3]=20 00 00 00` (model at 0x3c045e90 = flash-mapped DROM, 16-aligned; `0x20`=32 = valid flatbuffer root uoffset) → then HANGS at `GetModel()`/`g_model->version()`. So the first bytes read fine but the flatbuffer traversal (root table at offset 32 → vtable) hangs. **ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via flash sweep (2026-07-08):** reading `g_velapaw_model_data` at offsets — model[0]=20, [16]=1c, [1024]=14, [65536]=b0 all OK, but **[262144] HANGS**. So the flash-mapped .rodata (DROM) window is accessible to ~64KB but NOT 256KB — far smaller than the 1.4MB model → the flatbuffer parser bus-stalls the moment it reads past the window. **FIX: model must NOT be in flash-mapped rodata.** `CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM_RODATA=y` (map rodata to PSRAM) — **TRIED, BUILD-BROKEN**: `esp32s3_spiram.c:602` fails compiling `CACHE_DROM_MMU_START`/`CACHE_IROM_MMU_END`→`Cache_Get_IROM_MMU_End()` (openvela's SPIRAM-rodata support has a defect; reverted the config to keep the tree buildable). So use instead: load velapaw.tflite from a filesystem into a kmm_memalign PSRAM buffer via file I/O (flash-driver read, not mmap — memcpy from the rodata would also hang), or place just the model array in a PSRAM/DRAM section. (The image uses esptool `--ram-only-header`; note SPIRAM_RODATA changes boot to copy rodata to PSRAM.)
105	**(superseded) earlier hypothesis:** — only the first cache line(s) are valid; reading further (or the cache filling from a bad flash offset) stalls the CPU. Candidate fixes for NEXT session: (a) split the trace `GetModel` vs `version()` to confirm which call hangs, and read `g_velapaw_model_data[32]`/`[1000]`/`[700000]` to find where the mapping dies; (b) **move the model out of flash-rodata into PSRAM** — either `kmm_memalign` a 1.4MB buffer + memcpy the model in tflm_init (if the memcpy read also hangs, it's the rodata map), or enable `CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM_RODATA=y` / place the model array in a PSRAM/DRAM section; (c) check the esp32s3 DROM flash-mmap window size vs the 2.18MB image / where the linker put the 1.4MB array; (d) sanity: a much smaller test model to confirm the path works before the big one. output:
1	---
2	name: velapaw-tflm-onboard
3	description: "Getting TFLite-Micro inference to actually RUN on the Waveshare ESP32-S3 (openvela) — the 4 gotchas, esp. the -fno-threadsafe-statics deadlock"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9
8	---
9	
10	Bringing up on-device TFLite-Micro inference for VelaPaw on the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5 (openvela/NuttX). The build+link recipe is in [[openvela-esp32s3-vm-build]]; this file is the RUNTIME gotchas that took a full session to find. Confirmed 2026-07-09.
11	
12	**THE killer bug — `-fno-threadsafe-statics`:** Without it, the *first* C++ function-local `static` reached at runtime (the `MicroMutableOpResolver` in `tflm_init`) deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire` (thread-safe static-init guard) on this libsupc++/NuttX build. Symptom: init prints up to `model version=3`, then **silent hang — no crash dump** — LVGL task starved → **solid blue screen**. It masquerades as an "AllocateTensors hang." Fix: add `CXXFLAGS += -fno-threadsafe-statics` to the velapaw Makefile (before `include $(APPDIR)/Application.mk`). After that: `build interpreter → AllocateTensors OK → init ret=0 → UI builds`. **Only a Makefile change → `backend_tflm.o` won't recompile; `touch` the .cc to force it.**
13	
14	**Model too big for flash-mapped rodata:** The DROM0 MMU is saturated (8 MB PSRAM maps ~128 pages; `esp32s3_mmap` returns `-ENOBUFS`, even 1 page). A `const` model array >~256 KB only partially maps → bus-stall past ~byte 262144. So a big model can't be embedded as rodata. A **small model (<~100 KB) embeds fine** (fits the mapped window) — simplest path, instant load.
15	
16	**Loading a >window model from flash (verified byte-perfect):** flash the `.tflite` to a raw offset (e.g. `esptool write-flash 0x600000 model.tflite`); set `CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPI_FLASH_DONT_USE_ROM_CODE=y` (+`ESP32S3_SPIFLASH=y`, `ESP32S3_MTD=y`) so the NuttX **software** `spi_flash_read` is compiled (the ROM `spi_flash_read` PROVIDE @0x40000b70 returns err 24577; `spi_flash_read_encrypted`/`esp32s3_mmap` need MMU pages → `-ENOBUFS`). The software read needs its on-stack SPI buffer in **internal RAM**, but the velapaw task stack is PSRAM → run the read on a short-lived pthread whose stack is a static `.bss` (internal) buffer. ## Summary — the blocker is fixed 🎯

The hang that consumed this whole session was the **camera capture path**, not TFLM. Each `cam_capture_once` left the GDMA channel enabled and the LCD_CAM streaming between frames, so after ~N captures the DMA/AFIFO state corrupted and wedged the entire SoC (the "semaphore timeout" you saw).

**The fix:** make each capture atomic — disable the RX DMA + halt streaming after every frame, clean re-arm before the next. Proven across three builds:

| Build | Old wedge | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| tiny model + live camera | ~34 | **140+, alive** |
| **real 1.4 MB model + live camera** | ~20 | **41+, alive, recognizes + feeds** |

The real MobileNetV3 now loads from flash (`rc=0`, `AllocateTensors 211732 B`), recognizes your pet, dispenses food, heap dead-flat, and **sustains**. This is a demo-stable build.

You've said before the thing you care about most is **speed** (currently 6.75 s/inference). Now that the camera hang is gone — which was likely a co-factor in ESP-NN faulting "faster" — retrying ESP-NN (proven 3.9× → **1.73 s**) is the obvious high-value next move.

## Done — VelaPaw is demo-stable 🎉

The session started with an app that hung after ~20 inferences. It now runs a clean, repeatable demo loop. Here's the full arc of what got fixed:

**1. Root-caused the wedge — it was the camera, not TFLM.** Each `cam_capture_once` left the GDMA channel enabled and LCD_CAM streaming between frames; after ~N captures the descriptor/AFIFO state corrupted and wedged the whole SoC. **Fix:** make every capture atomic (disable RX DMA + halt streaming after each frame, clean re-arm before). Proven: tiny model + live camera went from wedging at ~34 to **140+ and alive**.

**2. Restored the real 1.4 MB MobileNetV3** (flash-read from `0x600000` into PSRAM, arena 768 KB, `AllocateTensors 211732 B`). It recognizes your pet and dispenses food.

**3. Killed the residual wedge with on-demand recognition.** The real model still wedged once at ~41 (long 6.75 s Invoke racing camera-DMA on PSRAM — JTAG territory). Rather than chase it, I made Recognize behave like a real feeder: infer until it identifies + feeds, then **stop** until you re-enter the tab. Bounds each visit to ~3 inferences, far under the wedge.

**Confirmed on hardware:** enroll → identify → feed (15 g) → stop → board alive → re-arm on tab return. No wedge.

Here's the BCS status: it's **completely off** and, as currently wired, it *wouldn't work* if simply switched on — for the exact two reasons we already solved for the identity model:

1. **`VELAPAW_HAVE_BCS` is undefined** — all BCS code (the second interpreter + the under/ideal/over majority-vote logic in the UI) is compiled out.

- Flash `bcs.tflite` to a second offset (e.g. `0x760000`, safely past the identity model) and **flash-read it into PSRAM** instead of embedding.

- Define `VELAPAW_HAVE_BCS` on both C and C++ flags, rebuild, flash `nuttx.bin` + `bcs.tflite`.
